title: Willow Finance risk-model-integration-call-notes
content:
Context:
- Intro call with Willow Finance (fraud & risk platform) to scope integrating their proprietary risk-scoring model with Redwood Private (VPC). They have strict data residency and audit requirements; evaluating a P0 private deployment with HSM-backed keys and no external logging.

Participants:
- Priya Rao (Redwood SE) - owner of integration
- Marcus Li (Redwood infra) - private deploy lead
- Daniel Hsu (Redwood runtime) - serving/runtime constraints
- Sara Kim (Willow) - product manager
- Rajiv Menon (Willow) - infra/ops lead

High-level goals from Willow:
1) Run their closed-source risk model (proprietary Transformer ~28B parameters) in their AWS account inside a private subnet (no internet egress).
2) Strict KMS/HSM usage for model keys and request-level envelope encryption; audit logs must be stored in their S3 with TTL 7 years.
3) Typical traffic: steady 75 req/s during business hours, spikes to 350 req/s during batch re-score windows. p95 latency target <= 200ms for 1K token inference (mainly short contexts + KV cache usage).
4) Must support canary rollouts and fast rollback; need per-customer A/B routing and traffic split.
5) Zero external logging of PII. Metrics only (aggregated) allowed; traces must be redacted.

Technical constraints and notes (from call):
- Model: Willow will provide a containerized model artifact that expects a specific tokenizer variant (not identical to HF default). We must validate tokenization locally before deploy.
- No outbound internet: installer must include all container images and kernel modules; use air-gapped bundle for on-prem install path.
- KMS/HSM: Willow uses AWS CloudHSM; Redwood must support using their HSM for signing model artifacts and for runtime key unwrap. Ensure minimal key material leaves HSM.
- Audit logs: Redwood control-plane events are OK but must be pushed to Willow's S3; Redwood must provide a signed digest of logs daily.
- Rate limiting: Willow wants soft throttles with burst allowance. Recommend token-bucket config: steady_rate=100 req/s, burst=400.
- Autoscale: Need fast scale-up for spikes; discussed pre-warming and reserve capacity. For Private, propose a warm pool of standby pods (3 nodes) to handle 3x baseline headroom.
- KV cache: model supports KV caching across requests for the same session; Willow's workflows reuse short prefixes a lot. Enable prefix caching but add TTL of 10 minutes for cached entries due to data retention policy.
- Streaming: Willow prefers non-streaming (single response) for quality and auditability; streaming can be disabled per-route.
- Metrics/telemetry: only CPU/GPU utilization, request latencies, error rates allowed. No token-level payload telemetry.

Integration gotchas flagged during discussion:
- Tokenization mismatch: Their tokenizer yields longer token counts vs HF; cost/latency estimates based on tokens will be off. Action: run tokenization reference suite with 500 typical requests to calibrate.
- Determinism: Their model has a custom temperature/sampling tweak; must ensure seed and deterministic inference for A/B comparison.
- Quantization: They asked about int8 quantization. Risk model team concerned about small distributional shifts. Proposed approach: run internal eval harness on 5k labeled cases comparing FP16 vs int8 (quality delta threshold 0.5% recall loss max).
- Storage of model artifacts: Willow requires checksum-signed artifacts with attestation. Redwood should support bundle signing and an attestation header in deployment API.
- Canary traffic & fallback: Need automatic fallback to smaller model variant if memory pressure triggers OOM; discuss fallback policy: fail-open vs fail-closed. Willow prefers fail-closed for risk decisions (reject if model unavailable).

Acceptance criteria (willow-defined):
- Deployment runs in their VPC, no egress, keys via CloudHSM; confirmation of 3-month audit export to S3 (sample logs).
- p95 latency <= 200ms at 75 req/s steady with 1K token typical requests with KV caching enabled.
- Canary mechanism: ability to route 1% -> 50% traffic with instant rollback < 2 minutes.
- No plaintext PII leaves environment (validated by on-site security review).

Recommended Redwood approach (initial plan):
1) Pre-work: obtain model artifact, tokenizer binary, and small eval dataset (500 queries + 1k labeled). Run tokenization and local perf profiling. (owner: Priya, due: 2025-11-09)
2) Build an air-gapped deployment bundle with all container images, runtime binaries, and kernel modules. Provide install checklist for Willow infra. (owner: Marcus, due: 2025-11-20)
3) Implement HSM integration prototype connecting Redwood control-plane to Willow CloudHSM (key unwrap flow). Minimal secret material flow diagram required. (owner: Daniel, due: 2025-12-05)
4) Eval: run FP16 vs int8 on 5k labeled cases, produce confusion matrices and delta on recall/precision. (owner: Priya + Willow ML team, due: 2025-12-12)
5) Canary plan: implement config to route traffic, collect aggregated metrics (no payload). Rollout runbook and rollback playbook. (owner: Priya + Marcus, due: 2025-12-20)

Action items (quick list):
- [Priya] Get artifact + tokenizer + sample dataset from Willow (ask for sample of worst-case long contexts) — due 2025-11-09.
- [Marcus] Start air-gapped bundle; list all required OS/kernel versions and NVIDIA driver pins — due 2025-11-20.
- [Daniel] Prototype CloudHSM unwrap and signed-deploy flow; create threat model doc for key handling — due 2025-12-05.
- [Willow: Rajiv] Share internal compliance checklist and S3 bucket/write policy for audit logs — due 2025-11-16.
- [Priya] Create tokenization calibration harness and run on 500 samples, report token inflation factor — due 2025-11-12.

Notes-to-self / follow-ups:
- Check licensing/TA for running closed-source model in customer VPC (legal review).
- Discuss with runtime team about forced fail-closed behavior; may need a lightweight policy shim in front of model.
- Confirm whether Redwood must do live attestation or signed digests are sufficient for Willow audit.
- Prepare a short one-pager for Willow CISO summarizing data flow, key handling, and audit guarantees.

Open questions (need answers from Willow):
1) Can Willow accept aggregated per-route metrics at 1-min granularity only, or do they want 10s? (affects telemetry implementation)
2) Will they allow temporary access for Redwood engineers (jumpbox) during initial install? They indicated "limited privileged access" but need exact scope.
3) Are there any legal constraints that prevent Redwood from holding any metadata about deployments? Some teams want zero metadata retention.

Miscellaneous:
- Potential performance improvement: explore cross-request KV sharing across correlated sessions (willow uses session identifiers mapped to user id). Need privacy check.
- Cost note: Private warm pool will add baseline monthly cost; finance will want an estimate before committing.

Next meeting: schedule install-readiness call the week of 2025-11-24. Priya to propose 3 slots.

Quick raw transcript snippets (paraphrased):
- Sara (Willow): "We cannot risk data exfiltration; HSM & air-gapped is non-negotiable."
- Rajiv (Willow): "Can you guarantee we can rollback within two minutes?"
- Daniel (Redwood): "We'll prototype a signed artifact flow and an attestation header so you can validate deploys."

End of notes.
summary: Call notes capturing Willow Finance requirements for private VPC deployment of proprietary risk model: HSM integration, air-gapped bundle, KV caching behavior, performance targets (p95<=200ms), canary/rollback needs, and a list of action items and open questions.
